messages:
sofia: Quick RFC follow-up — org vs project token convergence. Wanted to surface the proposal and get alignment before we draft the migration RFC. TL;DR: introduce project-scoped ephemeral tokens (brokered exchange) + org-level long-lived keys as a fallback during transition. Questions: SDK exchange pattern, RBAC mapping, private/Dedicated compatibility, audit/rotation. Planning a staged rollout next quarter.

mike: +1 on brokered exchange. main worry is client churn. we should add an SDK helper that does the exchange transparently (middleware). example usage: `const token = await sdk.exchangeOrgKeyForProjectToken(orgKey, projectId)` then use `Authorization: Bearer <ephemeral>` in requests. Endpoint: `POST /v1/token/exchange` -> returns `{ token, expires_at }`.

leo: Important: RBAC semantics must be explicit. my suggestion: keep roles at org granularity, but allow project-scoped bindings that narrow permissions. sample policy: ```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "bindings": [
    { "role": "viewer", "scope": "org:123" },
    { "role": "model-infer", "scope": "project:proj-42", "conditions": { "max_qps": 50 } }
  ]
}
```
This lets a project token carry narrower rights and also embed simple rate restrictions.

anika: ops/infra concerns: token exchange increases load on the auth broker. need autoscale rules + rate limits per org to avoid blast radius. for Private deployments, prefer workload-identity (no long-lived org keys) where the exchange is local to the VPC and backed by customer KMS/HSM. also need clear rotation story: org keys rotate monthly by default, ephemeral tokens short (5-15m).

security-bot: system: token-exchange endpoint scanned: no high-severity issues flagged in static scan (SAST). recommend adding e2e tests for delegated claims.

sofia: Proposed migration steps: 1) add `/v1/token/exchange` and short-lived token format (JWT-ish with `project_id`, `issued_for`, `exp`) 2) add SDK middleware + http client helpers 3) rollout canary: route 10% service traffic through exchange for 2 weeks 4) enable audit logging & metric dashboards 5) flip default issuance to ephemeral and deprecate org-key use after 3 months (with kill-switch). Need sign-off on step 3 load caps and step 5 timeline.

mike: tiny addition: token binding claim schema example: `claims: { "project_id": "proj-42", "issued_for": "svc-ingest", "delegation": [] }` and we should validate `issued_for` against service registry. also: SDK fallback flows when exchange fails (retry/backoff + circuit-breaker).

leo: one more ops question: cross-project calls where a service operating in project A needs to call a model in project B — propose `actor` claim + `delegation_chain` array (each element = `{actor_id, scope, issued_at}`) so auditors can reconstruct. sample claim: ```json
"delegation_chain": [{"actor":"svc-a","scope":"project:proj-a","issued_at":1680000000},{"actor":"svc-b","scope":"project:proj-b","issued_at":1680000100}]
```
That lets enforcement evaluate both direct and upstream permissions.

anika: I can write the rollout playbook and update runbooks for Dedicated/Private. action items for me: list services that perform direct model calls (ingest, realtime-proxy, batch-worker), estimate exchange RPS, and propose autoscale limits. tagging: @mike @leo please drop service lists here.

sofia: awesome — thanks. can we aim to have the draft migration RFC + SDK proposal by EOD next Wed? I'll schedule a short triage meeting after the draft. Also thinking about a compatibility header when both token types are accepted: `X-Auth-Mode: ephemeral|org`.

mike: sounds good, will add SDK sketch. :thumbsup:

leo: ok, I'll write the RBAC policy appendix and cross-project delegation section.

anika: will do the playbook and perf estimates.

security-bot: reminder: create evaluation alert rule for any unexpected 5xx rate > 0.5% on the token-exchange path during canary.

sofia: noted. thanks everyone — will ping again once the draft is up.
